problem: Recovery stampede: append-only recovery attempt IDs allow multiple workers to start recovery for the same stale opportunity before they can observe each other.
acceptance: Concurrent recovery candidates for one opportunity yield exactly one active recovery owner.
Recovery collision losers stop before target writes and preserve immutable collision evidence.
Late original returns remain reconcilable and are never discarded.
Recovery ownership can expire or be safely superseded so a crashed recovery does not become a permanent lock.
No Current, Human Accepted, Served, or global promotion authority is granted.
title: Single-winner recovery ownership pin
mission: Extend the existing lease/retry recovery substrate with a host-safe create-if-absent ownership pin keyed by opportunity/recovery generation so only one eligible recovery may enter active execution at a time. Reuse the existing stale scanner, overlap/CAS checks, late-return reconciliation and discovery-style atomic pin semantics; preserve every losing recovery attempt as evidence without allowing it to mutate target bytes.

incident_repair.reason: A durable Kernel recovery run reached LIVE_RECOVERY_COLLISION after a second recovery claim/run appeared, then exited before target writes. The collision was safely contained but consumed a worker and created avoidable recovery lineage noise.

human_friction_reduction.reason: Mass /wc capacity should convert into distinct useful durable work rather than repeated recoveries of the same blocker; a single-winner recovery pin moves collision handling ahead of STARTED and target inspection.

regression_prevention.reason: The existing lease/retry candidate correctly parks on active overlap and preserves late returns, but recovery claims themselves are append-only unique IDs. A separate ownership pin can prevent simultaneous active recovery while retaining the existing immutable evidence model.

falsification: Reject or merge this proposal if current repository-host recovery execution already proves a create-if-absent single-owner primitive that is acquired before any recovery claim/run becomes active. The observed 09:51 Kernel collision and 09:55/09:56 Facultad recovery overlap are direct counterevidence to that condition unless a newer artifact supersedes them.
